title: Entirely nonlocal quantum magic without entanglement
authors: Fuchuan Wei, Ruixia Wang, Yujia Zhang, Huihui Li, Junfeng Li, Fei Yan, Zi-Wen Liu
abstract: Nonstabilizerness, or magic, is an archetypal \emph{quantum} resource that is necessary for quantum computational advantage. Here we uncover a phenomenon seemingly at odds with the quantum nature of magic: entirely nonlocal magic (ENM)---magic present only in correlations and absent from each party's marginal---can live without entanglement. We systematically study this separation and show it is universal and operationally reversible: every magical state or channel can be encoded into and recovered from a separable ENM realization using only local stabilizer processing and classical communication. We leverage this mechanism to devise an activation key protocol in which a classical key controls access to non-Clifford operations. We further formulate magic secret sharing, in which computational power inaccessible to any party alone becomes accessible through cooperation. On a superconducting quantum processor, we experimentally demonstrate activation key and network computing primitives, together with separable ENM state preparation and extraction protocols. Together, our results establish that magic can be classically activated, localized, and secret-shared without entanglement, providing new resource-control primitives for distributed quantum computation.
summary: This paper introduces and experimentally verifies Entirely Nonlocal Magic (ENM), a quantum resource that carries magic only in correlations, not locally, and crucially, without entanglement. The authors develop protocols to use ENM for classical key-controlled activation of non-Clifford operations and for magic secret sharing. This establishes a new paradigm for controlling quantum computational power in distributed quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates Entirely Nonlocal Magic (ENM), a quantum resource where nonstabilizerness exists only in global correlations and not locally, and demonstrates that this magic can be controlled without relying on entanglement.
main_result: They show that magic can be classically activated, localized, and secret-shared using separable ENM states, providing new resource-control primitives for distributed quantum computation.
method: The study involves systematic construction of separable ENM states and channels, followed by experimental demonstrations of activation key protocols and magic secret sharing on a superconducting quantum processor.
model_or_system: The work is demonstrated on a superconducting quantum processor, utilizing bipartite and multipartite separable quantum states ($ho^{(n)}_\psi$, $ho^{(n)}_T$) and channels.
key_observables: Robustness of Magic (RoM), Choi-state log-RoM ($L_R$), and state/process fidelities.
important_parameters: The analysis considers scaling with the number of qubits ($n$) and the parameter $\alpha$ in the Pauli-moment functional $M_\alpha$.
main_assumptions: The protocols rely fundamentally on the availability of local stabilizer processing and classical communication.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate ENM in separable states/channels, the Magic Activation Key switching between locked/activated modes, and the implementation of Magic Secret Sharing.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework for ENM, then develops protocols for activation keys and secret sharing, and finally provides experimental demonstrations on superconducting hardware, supplemented by theoretical scaling analyses using Pauli moments.
why_interesting: It provides a novel mechanism to control quantum computational power (magic) using only classical control and separable resources, which is highly relevant for understanding resource management in distributed quantum computing architectures.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Entirely nonlocal magic without entanglement. In a separable bipartite state or channel, magic can be encoded entirely in correlations while both local reductions remain magic-free. Cooperation using stabilizer operations and clas- sical communication recovers the hidden resource.

FIG. 2. Magic activation key. A classical secret key switches a Clifford+T processor between a magic-free locked mode and n activated mode that restores the intended computation, without quantum communication or shared entanglement. (a) In the locked mode, each protected T gate use implements either T or T ⊥:= ZT according to the key unknown to the user. Without the key, hidden randomization (possibly correlated across gates) makes user’s effective protected dynamics a stabilizer channel. (b) Once the key bit bi is revealed, the user applies the Pauli correction Zbi after the corresponding protected gate, restoring the intended T operation. FIG. 3. Magic secret sharing with two-way T-type ENM links. (a) Three separable ENM links (green) connect mea- surement node A to computational node B. Measuring the link qubits at A in the X basis and postselecting on X = +1 for all three, with the outcomes communicated to B, localizes three |T⟩states at B. These states are consumed to imple- ment CS on two target qubits at B. (b) The standard T-state injection gadget JT .
